newsitem.title: USA: Florida seeks reversal on hurricane center cuts.
newsitem.headline: Florida seeks reversal on hurricane center cuts.

text.p: Two forecasters at the National Hurricane Center have received staff reduction notices, part of a federal budget cut that eliminates 11 positions, or 22 percent, from the center's staff, a spokesman said Wednesday.
"Reduction-in-force letters have in fact gone out. And two of our people got them," said Center spokesman Frank Lapore.

Residents of Florida and other coastal states have been up in arms since last month, when they learned that Washington was cutting 11 jobs from the workforce at the Center, which is responsible for posting hurricane watches and warnings to coastal areas during the six-month Atlantic hurricane season.

Last year, the center, which also monitors hurricanes around the world, tracked 13 tropical storms and hurricanes in the Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea. In 1995, it tracked 19 in a season that was the busiest in six decades.
In an "average" June-through-November Atlantic hurricane season there are 9.3 tropical storms, of which 5.8 become hurricanes, with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (119 kph) or higher.

Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles has just sent a letter to U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley thanking him for federal officials' recent assurances that Florida's 14 million residents would not be at greater risk because of the cuts, but saying he was not convinced.

"I am very concerned that the budget cutbacks are undermining the effectiveness of the warning systems, thereby putting our people at risk. I stand by my people in asking that you ease this peril," he said.
Emergency workers contend a smaller hurricane center could mean unnecessary evacuations and less accurate forecasts.
Florida Congressman E. Clay Shaw has introduced legislation to restore funding cut from the National Weather Service budget. And the U.S. Senate has scheduled hearings on the issue for April 28.
The hurricane center expects to have 39 workers on June 1, when the 1997 Atlantic season begins.
